mode: User-authorized wgpu scene/pixel checks, window-free egui regression suite and strict linting. No native desktop window was launched during this change.

gui.scope: Includes a new regression for plain Classic, ruled Classic and Studio at light/scale 1 and dark/scale 2, repeated layout, before/after actual two-axis wheel panning. No scroll-fade gradient mesh overlays the canvas, and caller scroll styling remains unchanged.

gpu_pixels.scope: The real frontend canvas wrappers paint a known opaque white fixture. Sixty actual framebuffer sample checks cover the center plus four clipped edges across the three presentations, two theme/density cases and pre/post-pan states. The fixture verifies both axes actually move and keeps its rendered test cursor outside samples.

gpu_scenes.scope: Complete application scenes render through wgpu in both themes. Archived 1100x900 Classic workspaces show removal of the right-edge gradient; OS title/menu bars are outside these exports. Before images are copied unchanged from the previous outline review record, whose source commit is 63b363f.

regression_baseline.result: The pre-fix headless probe detects a scroll-edge gradient. The actual GPU sample at Classic scale 1, point [377,150], is [254,254,254,255] rather than opaque white [255,255,255,255].
regression_baseline.probe_scope: Initial overflow assertions before panning; later pan-origin assertions and test-cursor handling were added after these baseline probes. Expected failures are archived separately from passing current logs.

scope: egui 0.37 scroll fades paint after canvas content and tint visible image pixels near clipped viewport edges. Both frontends now disable the fade locally; Studio has its own stable presentation scope so caller scroll cues remain unaffected. Classic plain/ruled views retain their shared presentation identity.
limits: Pixel checks use an opaque white chrome fixture, not every image color or native window/driver path. Full application scene exports are visually reviewed, not a complete Windows fidelity qualification. Native menus, pen/IME, sustained-input latency and remaining roadmap requirements remain open.
